newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends up on uncertainty over outflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends up on uncertainty over outflows.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday at around 7.5 percent, up from the previous close of 4.0-4.5 but off the intraday high of 9.5-10.0 percent on uncertainty over funds outflows from banks, dealers said.
They said stray deals were reported at 10.0 percent but most of the day's trade was between 7.5 and 8.5 percent.
Dealers said call money rates moved up on Friday on uncertainty over liquidity conditions following subscription to a state government bond issue on Wednesday.
The money market was inactive on Thursday as banks in the commercial capital of Bombay and most other centres were closed for local holidays.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) offered 10-year state government bonds worth 25 billion rupees for sale on April 30 and dealers said they expected the issue to be heavily subscribed.

"I think it is a foregone conclusion that the issue will be fully-subscribed," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "What is more important is to know the amount of excess bids received by the RBI and how much it is retaining."
The RBI had not issued details on the bond sale results till late Friday evening.
Dealers said the uncertainty over the amount of outflows led to higher call money rates on Friday.
"Lenders took full opportunity of the lack of information to drive up rates today," said a dealer.
Dealers said prices of government securities fell in light trade on Friday as market players reacted to the higher call rates by selling.
"It (the fall in prices) was the usual reaction to higher call money rates," said a dealer. "But volumes were poor."
He said trades were worth around 1.37 billion rupees against Wednesday's 2.13 billion.
Prices fell for securities of all maturities, dealers said.
They said the 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock dropped 101.60 rupees from 101.90, the 13.50 percent 1998 to 102.75 from 103 and 13.40 percent 1999 to 104.70 from 105.25.
Other securities which registered a decline in prices were the 13.80 percent 200 which dropped to 105.70 from 105.90 and the 13.05 percent 2007 to 100.70 from 101, dealers said.
